analysis.investment_thesis: Aequs trades at 288x EV/EBITDA and 10x P/S on a business that is persistently loss-making, generating deeply negative free cash flow (–₹239 Cr in FY25), and showing zero ROCE to speak of. The market has priced in flawless execution of a multi-year turnaround while the operating reality continues to deteriorate — a textbook case of paying for a dream at a nightmare price.
key_strengths: Vertically integrated aerospace & consumer goods cluster model with genuine barriers to replication
Promoter holds 59% — meaningful skin in the game
Gross margin of 56% suggests the underlying product mix has pricing power if overhead is controlled
key_risks: Extreme valuation (EV/EBITDA 288x) leaves zero margin of safety — any execution stumble is catastrophic for shareholders
FCF destruction is worsening: –₹76 Cr → –₹175 Cr → –₹239 Cr; CWIP surged to ₹395 Cr with no visible return timeline
Revenue stagnated/declined (₹965 Cr → ₹925 Cr) while net losses re-widened to –₹102 Cr in FY25 — the investment cycle is not yielding growth yet
red_flags: Forward P/E of 1,140x — the business would need to generate ~₹10 Cr net profit at current price just to justify a 1,000x multiple; actual profits are deeply negative
Three consecutive years of net losses; ROCE of only 1.11% on a heavily asset-intensive business
Operating income collapsed from ₹163 Cr (FY24) to ₹57 Cr (FY25) — EBITDA margin compression is severe, not cyclical
Negative other income of –₹6 Cr in FY25 vs +₹44 Cr in FY24 masks underlying weakness in prior-year reported numbers
Market cap of ₹11,202 Cr vs total equity of ₹717 Cr = P/B of 12.85x for a loss-making industrial company with negative retained earnings as recently as FY24
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aequs is a genuinely interesting industrial cluster concept — aerospace, toys, and consumer goods manufacturing under one integrated ecosystem in Belgaum. The business model has real long-term logic. But as I always say, the question is never "is this a good company?" — it is "what does the price already reflect?" At 288x EV/EBITDA and 10x revenue, the market has already paid for 10+ years of successful execution. With operating income declining 56% year-over-year (₹163 Cr → ₹57 Cr), FCF worsening every year, and CWIP ballooning to ₹395 Cr, there is no fundamental anchor for this valuation today.

The balance sheet tells a concerning story: the company raised equity (reserves swung from –₹15 Cr to +₹135 Cr via FY24 equity infusion), yet still burned ₹239 Cr of free cash in FY25. Debt remains ₹785 Cr with finance costs of ₹64 Cr — consuming more than the entire operating cash flow. The CWIP build is a bet that these clusters eventually attract anchor tenants and generate returns, but that is a multi-year, high-uncertainty thesis. Risk here is asymmetric in the wrong direction: the downside in a re-rating scenario (to, say, 3–4x revenue, a reasonable terminal multiple for an industrial services company) implies a price closer to ₹30–50 — an 70–80% loss. The upside requires near-perfect execution on an unproven model. That is not the kind of bet I want to make.
